## What the approval is tied to

Content hash `853445054e584581996e897830e24480b2d9d2d30904aeb385bcd84cf56e9508`

The vocabulary currently hashes to the same value, so the words below are the words the attestation covers.

The hash is taken over every key, its term AND its note, sorted by key. The
note is included because that is where the clinical boundary lives — "recorded
is not delivered", "opened is not reviewed". Changing a single word in any
note changes the hash and invalidates the approval.

## Scope

The clinician-facing words shown in place of raw event keys in the audit and activity views of a person's record, and the note beside each one saying what it does and does not mean.

Appears on:

- `/clinician/member/[id]/audit`
- `/clinician/activity`
- `/review/audit`

## What this approval does NOT cover

- The clinical rules the events describe. These are words for things that already happened; no threshold, gate or safety precedence was reviewed or changed.
- The events themselves. Which events are recorded, and what they contain, is unchanged by this approval.
- Any patient-facing wording. Every term here is written for a clinician who can open the evidence underneath it.
- Any authorisation for real-person care, public enrollment, or payer deployment. The release boundary is unchanged.
- Event keys not listed in the document. An unlisted key renders as its raw value and is marked as carrying no approved words.

## The approved words (86)

The raw key is retained everywhere the term is shown — the term is what the
column displays, the key stays one disclosure away.

| Event key | Clinician-facing term | What it means, and what it does not |
|---|---|---|
| `alert_closed` | Safety alert closed | A clinician closed a safety alert with a documented action. |
| `alert_reviewed` | Safety alert reviewed | A clinician reviewed a safety alert. Reviewing is not closing. |
| `attention_signal_acknowledged` | Attention signal acknowledged | A clinician marked that they had seen this signal. Acknowledging is not reviewing and decides nothing. |
| `attention_signal_state_changed` | Attention signal changed state | The signal moved between states under the attention policy. The policy decided this, not a person. |
| `autonomous_rule_signoff` | Automated rule signed off | A named reviewer signed off an automated rule. |
| `autopilot_outreach` | Automated outreach sent | The product sent a scheduled message. Sending is not reading, and no reply is implied. |
| `between_visit_care_action` | Between-visit action recorded | Something done between visits was recorded. |
| `between_visit_care_action_corrected` | Between-visit action corrected | A between-visit record was corrected. The original stays readable beside the correction. |
| `care_handoff_proposed` | Transfer of accountability proposed | One clinician asked another to take over. The person who proposed it remains accountable until it is accepted. |
| `care_handoff_resolved` | Transfer of accountability answered | The proposed transfer was accepted, declined or withdrawn. The detail says which. |
| `care_track_archived` | Care path archived | A care path was closed. The record of it stays; only its active status changed. |
| `care_track_selected` | Care path selected | A care path was chosen for this person. Paths are optional and the programme runs without one. |
| `checkin_safety_positive` | Safety item answered on a check-in | The person answered a safety item in a way the policy treats as requiring a response. It is an obligation to respond, not a conclusion about them. |
| `clinical_memory_item_corrected` | Approved memory corrected | An item of approved clinical memory was corrected. The original stays readable beside it. |
| `clinical_override` | Clinical override recorded | A clinician overrode an automated decision, with a reason on the record. |
| `clinical_record_corrected` | Record corrected | A clinical record was corrected. Both what was believed then and what is believed now keep their answers. |
| `clinical_review_approved` | Clinical review approved | A named clinician approved something that required clinical review. The approval covers what was put in front of them, not the surrounding work. |
| `clinical_thread_connection_accepted` | Suggested connection accepted | A clinician accepted a suggested connection between records. The suggestion is not evidence; their acceptance is the decision. |
| `clinical_thread_connection_rejected` | Suggested connection rejected | A clinician rejected a suggested connection. The suggestion stays on the record with their answer. |
| `clinical_thread_connection_revisited` | Connection decision revisited | A clinician returned to a connection they had already answered. |
| `clinical_thread_created` | Clinical thread created | A thread was opened to follow one line of clinical thinking. A thread groups thinking; it is not a clinical finding and decides nothing. |
| `clinician_ask_answered` | Question answered from the record | An evidence-linked answer was produced from information this clinician is authorised to see. An answer is assistance, not an approved record. |
| `clinician_ask_scope_violation` | Question refused: outside permitted scope | An answer was refused because it would have drawn on something this clinician may not see. The refusal is the safe outcome, not an error. |
| `clinician_thought_captured` | Working note captured | A working note was captured, by voice or by typing. |
| `clinician_thought_discarded` | Working note discarded | A working note was discarded before anything was approved from it. |
| `clinician_thought_items_saved` | Note items approved into memory | A clinician reviewed proposed items and approved them as reusable clinical memory. Nothing becomes memory without that review. |
| `clinician_thought_organized` | Working note organised | A clinician rearranged their own working note. Nothing clinical changed. |
| `clinician_thought_saved` | Working note saved | A working note was saved. Saving is not filing and not signing. |
| `clinician_thought_started` | Working note started | A clinician began a working note. Working notes are theirs and are not part of the clinical record until filed. |
| `clinician_thought_written` | Working note written | A clinician typed a working note rather than speaking it. Both produce the same kind of note, and neither is part of the clinical record until items are approved from it. |
| `clinician_thoughts_opened` | Notes opened | A clinician opened the notes workspace. Opening changes nothing. |
| `clinician_transcript_corrected` | Transcript corrected | A clinician corrected a transcription. The original stays readable. |
| `command_context_opened` | Person opened from the work queue | A clinician opened this record from Command Center. Opening is not acknowledgement. |
| `companion_daily_chat_opened` | Companion opened | The person opened the companion. Opening changes nothing clinical. |
| `companion_memory_deleted` | Companion memory deleted | The person deleted what the companion remembered. This is their choice and needs no clinical reason. |
| `companion_message` | Companion message | A message passed between the person and the companion. The companion sets no clinical urgency and grants no access. |
| `companion_weekly_capped` | Companion weekly limit reached | The person reached the weekly companion limit. It is a usage limit, not a clinical judgement about them. |
| `contact_attempt_recorded` | Contact attempt recorded | A clinician recorded that they tried to make contact, and what happened. It is not proof that anything was delivered or received. |
| `demo_patient_created` | Fabricated person created | A fabricated person was created for demonstration. Nobody real is involved. |
| `export_created` | Export prepared | An export of records was prepared. Preparing is not sending, and nothing left the product because this row exists. |
| `export_download_refused` | Export download refused | A download was refused. The refusal is the control working, not an error. |
| `export_downloaded` | Export downloaded | A prepared export was downloaded. This is the point at which data left the product; preparing one does not. |
| `export_out_of_scope` | Export refused: outside permitted scope | An export was refused because it reached beyond what the requester may see. Nothing was produced. |
| `export_signature_invalid` | Export refused: signature did not verify | An export's signature did not verify, so it was refused. Treat the file as untrustworthy rather than merely stale. |
| `gate_safety_item_fired` | Safety rule applied | A safety rule restricted what happens next. The rule decided this; nothing on a reading screen can change, clear or add to it. |
| `intervention_confirmed` | Intervention confirmed | A clinician confirmed an intervention as recorded. Confirming is standing behind the record of what was done; it is not a statement about what followed it. |
| `intervention_record_opened` | Intervention record opened | A clinician opened the intervention record. Opening is not reviewing and changes nothing. |
| `intervention_recorded` | Intervention recorded | What was done with this person was written down. Recording is not a claim about what followed it. |
| `intervention_remapped` | Intervention reclassified | An intervention was moved to a different classification. Both the original and the correction stay readable. |
| `lesson_read` | Lesson read | The person opened a lesson. Reading is not improvement. |
| `login_failed` | Sign-in failed | A sign-in attempt failed. It says nothing about who was typing. |
| `login_locked` | Sign-in paused after repeated failures | Sign-in was paused for fifteen minutes after ten failures. A paused account is not a disengaged person. |
| `module_override_closed` | Module left closed by decision | A clinician declined to open a gated module, with a reason the person can read. |
| `module_override_opened` | Module opened by decision | A clinician opened a gated module with a reason the person can read. It relaxes the clinician gate only — the daily check-in, the cooldown, the per-day cap and the kill switch all still apply. |
| `note_draft_assembled` | Note draft assembled | Approved items were assembled into a draft to take into the record system. Steady does not sign it — a signature attests to a clinician's own statement. |
| `person_care_opened` | Care opened | A clinician opened the care section. Opening changes nothing. |
| `person_course_opened` | Course opened | A clinician opened the course landing. Opening changes nothing. |
| `person_record_viewed` | Record opened | Somebody opened this person's record. Opening is not treatment and not review; it is the access itself being recorded. |
| `pilot_terms_accepted` | Pilot terms accepted | The person accepted a named version of the pilot terms. What may be recorded about them follows the version they accepted, not the current one. |
| `pilot_terms_declined` | Pilot terms declined | The person declined the current pilot terms. Declining is a valid answer and is not a clinical event. |
| `post_session_check` | Post-session check recorded | What was observed after a session was recorded. Things in the same period are context, and context is not cause. |
| `practice_completed` | Practice completed | The person completed a practice. Use is not improvement. |
| `program_plan_generated` | Programme draft generated | A draft programme was produced. A draft is a suggestion until a clinician approves it, and generation is not approval. |
| `recovery_trajectory_opened` | Trajectory opened | A clinician opened the trajectory screen. Opening changes nothing. |
| `release_gate_signoff_stale` | Sign-off out of date | A recorded sign-off no longer matches the evidence it was given against, so it no longer counts as approval. |
| `return_goal_confirmed` | Life goal confirmed | A clinician confirmed the goal as written. |
| `return_goal_created` | Life goal recorded | A goal was written down in the person's own words. |
| `return_goal_observation_decided` | Proposed observation answered | A clinician accepted or rejected a proposed observation. A proposal is not evidence until somebody answers it. |
| `return_goal_observation_recorded` | Observation recorded against a goal | Something observed was attached to a goal. The source — the person's report or a clinician's observation — is on the record. |
| `return_goals_opened` | Life goals opened | A clinician opened the goals screen. Opening changes nothing. |
| `review_completed` | Review completed | A clinician recorded that they reviewed this and what they decided. It records their judgement, not an outcome, and it does not close whatever the work was about. |
| `review_note_status` | Review note status changed | The status of a review note changed. It does not change any clinical decision the note describes. |
| `screening_risk_item` | Risk item on a scored measure | A risk item on an instrument was answered in a way that requires a response. The instrument's own scale decides this, not a clinician's reading of it. |
| `screening_submitted` | Measure completed | The person completed a scored instrument. The score is on its own validated scale and is not combined with any other. |
| `session_hard_stop` | Session stopped by a safety rule | A rule stopped a session in progress. The rule decided this; the stop is not a judgement about the person. |
| `session_prepared` | Session prepared | A session was set up. Preparation is not a session. |
| `session_spoken_response` | Spoken response recorded | A spoken response was recorded during a session. |
| `session_started` | Session started | The person began a session. Starting is not completing, and nothing here says how it went. |
| `therapeutic_load_opened` | Load and readiness opened | A clinician opened the load screen. Opening changes nothing, and nothing on that screen restricts access. |
| `therapeutic_load_reviewed` | Load and readiness reviewed | A clinician recorded their reading of load and readiness. |
| `trajectory_reviewed` | Trajectory reading reviewed | A clinician agreed, disagreed or corrected a reading. The original reading stays on the record beside their answer. |
| `trajectory_snapshot_saved` | Trajectory reading stored | A reading was stored so it can be reproduced later from the same evidence, cutoff and policy version. It describes recorded observations and forecasts nothing. |
| `trigger_mapped_in_session` | Trigger mapped in session | A trigger was mapped during a session. Mapping records a connection the work surfaced; it is not a cause. |
| `trigger_updated` | Trigger updated | The person updated what they identified as a trigger, in their own words. It is the person's own account, not a clinician's observation. |
| `unlock_requested` | Module request made | The person asked for a gated module to be opened. Asking is not opening; it waits for a clinician's decision and reason. |
| `work_assigned` | Work assigned | Ownership of this work was recorded against somebody. Nobody was notified — there is no delivery path in this build. |

## Anything not listed here

An event key absent from this table renders as its raw value and is marked on
screen as carrying no approved words. It is not guessed at, and it is not
covered by this approval.
